candidates.label: Stress cardiomyopathy (Takotsubo syndrome) triggered by COVID-19 infection, with hypokalemia-induced QT prolongation leading to cardiac arrest
COVID-19 associated myocardial injury with transient left ventricular dysfunction and hypokalemia-induced QT prolongation causing cardiac arrest
Hypokalemia-induced ventricular arrhythmia (torsades de pointes) with cardiac arrest, with concurrent COVID-19 infection and stress cardiomyopathy
Acute coronary syndrome due to mild coronary artery disease

response.rationale: The patient's presentation with cardiac arrest, prolonged QTc, hypokalemia, and transient severe LV dysfunction with recovery, in the setting of COVID-19 infection and elevated inflammatory markers, without evidence of myocarditis or ischemia on MRI, strongly supports stress cardiomyopathy (Takotsubo) as the primary diagnosis. Hypokalemia likely contributed to QT prolongation and arrhythmia. Myocarditis and ACS are ruled out by MRI and angiography findings.
